Fix rotate with partial dropdowns (C core snap module change)

blockers.description: Snap module 0xFF sentinel means Global registers don't participate in Sync mode. C core spu94_snap.c needs a fallback subdivision parameter or state field so 0xFF resolves to global instead of being skipped.
blockers.workaround: Set all 4 dropdowns explicitly (not Global) before using Sync/Rotate

blockers.description: GUI-layer resolution of 0xFF to global caused register overwrites when BPM was unset in C core (tempo_bpm=0 makes spu94_set_subdivision fail). Two attempts reverted.

decisions.decision: Wall distance knobs are interactive, not read-only indicators
decisions.rationale: User wants to shape individual walls in Room Designer. Clamped by mBASE buffer boundary, not by Room Size.

decisions.decision: Buffer knob inverted in GUI (up=max space, down=crush)
decisions.rationale: Macro engine position 0 = mBASE at floor = max space, which is unintuitive. GUI inverts so up=max.
Already in toolbar, redundant. User confirmed they were cluttering the UI.

decisions.decision: Manual register changes refresh Spread+Sweep references
decisions.rationale: Without this, Echo Physics Sweep operates on old preset references, not the user's custom wall settings.

decisions.decision: Knob positions only sync from derived atomics on derive-all events
decisions.rationale: Timer-driven sync every 33ms caused knobs to snap back to stale derived values. knobsNeedSync flag gates updates to preset load and view switch only.

next_action: Fix the sync mode snap-to-0 bug by adding a global_subdivision field to spu94_state (C core) so the snap module can resolve 0xFF to the global subdivision instead of skipping. Then re-test Sync toggle + Rotate with partial dropdowns.
context_notes: Two attempts at GUI-layer resolution of 0xFF Global were reverted — both caused register overwrites. The fix must live in the C core where the snap module can resolve 0xFF at apply time using a state-level fallback subdivision. This is ~15 lines in spu94_snap.c + a new uint8_t field in spu94_state_internal.h + a setter function.
